bibliographic.title: Privacy, ethics, transparency, and accountability in AI systems for wearable devices
bibliographic.citation_apa: Radanliev, P. (2025). Privacy, ethics, transparency, and accountability in AI systems for wearable devices. Frontiers in Digital Health, 7, 1431246. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2025.1431246

methodology.method_family: systematic examination of ethical/regulatory challenges; privacy framework analysis; empirical assessment of publicly available datasets; data-driven methodological framework development
methodology.sample_description: publicly available datasets used for empirical assessment of model performance disparities
methodology.technology_context: AI and machine learning integrated into wearable sensor technologies for continuous monitoring, personalised interventions, and predictive analytics; models include CNN, RNN, random forests, gradient-boosted trees, and other ML/DL techniques

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article strongly addresses privacy, ethics, transparency, accountability, bias, and regulatory alignment for AI in regulated healthcare wearables, but the provided text does not focus on conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or LLM-based systems. It is better suited as supporting governance evidence than as central evidence for conversational LLM governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: High automated screening score may overstate fit because governance terms are present while conversational AI and LLM-specific governance are largely absent from the provided text.

appraisal.notes: Provided excerpts show a clear objective and proposed framework, but detailed study design, dataset enumeration, analysis procedures, results, and limitations are not sufficiently visible in the supplied text for stronger methodological appraisal.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent and relevant to AI governance in regulated healthcare wearables, but methodological detail and direct relevance to conversational LLM governance are limited in the evidence provided.

coding.theme: Governance of AI in wearable healthcare through privacy, ethics, transparency, and accountability
coding.subtheme: Operational ethical framework for ML/DL wearable health systems

synthesis.main_claim: AI and ML in wearable healthcare raise major privacy, bias, transparency, and accountability risks, and these can be addressed through a data-driven framework that embeds ethical principles and regulatory alignment across AI development stages.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a replicable framework operationalising transparency, accountability, explainable AI, bias mitigation, and consent-aware processing for wearable healthcare AI, aligned with GDPR, UK Data Protection Act, and EU AI Act.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on governance principles, privacy, ethics, transparency, accountability, bias mitigation, and regulatory alignment in regulated healthcare AI; not as central evidence for conversational or LLM-specific governance.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed journal article with identifiable bibliographic metadata.
Study focuses on AI/ML in wearable sensor technologies for healthcare, not conversational systems.
evidence.excerpt: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into wearable sensor technologies has substantially advanced health data science

evidence.claim: Article addresses privacy, ethics, transparency, accountability, bias, and regulatory concerns.

evidence.claim: Methods include analysis of privacy frameworks and empirical assessment of publicly available datasets.

evidence.claim: Study identifies demographic disparities in model performance.
evidence.excerpt: identifies significant disparities in model performance across demographic groups

evidence.claim: Proposes a data-driven methodological framework embedding transparency, accountability, and regulatory alignment.
